spec_features.spec_quote: we DO allow the agent to *voluntarily* stop by calling a `give_up(summary)` / `submit_conclusion(summary)` tool
spec_features.evidence: give_up is real end-to-end: schema at tools.py:104-122, handler _t_give_up at tools.py:231-232, loop sets gave_up when tc.name=='give_up' (agent_loop.py:181-182) then breaks (agent_loop.py:190-191). BUT submit_conclusion has NO schema and NO handler anywhere; it appears only in a config comment (config.py:35) and DESIGN.md:120/152. So only one of the two claimed exit tools exists.
spec_features.notes: give_up is fully honored as a stop; submit_conclusion is unimplemented. Marking partial because the claim names two tools and only one is wired.

spec_features.spec_quote: The loop runs for up to `max_turns` agent turns (default **20**
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:129 `for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns):` directly bounds the agent loop; default max_turns=20 at config.py:30. Termination defaults to 'max_turns' (agent_loop.py:58). The cap is the loop range itself, so it actually stops execution.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 20  # 10-20 per request; one model completion = one turn

spec_features.spec_quote: If the agent calls `give_up`/`submit_conclusion`, we stop and record an early termination
spec_features.evidence: On give_up the loop sets tr.termination = 'gave_up' and breaks (agent_loop.py:190-191), so it both stops AND records the early termination. Recorded value is serialized in the transcript. Again, only give_up is wired; submit_conclusion does not exist.
spec_features.notes: Stop + record genuinely implemented for give_up; submit_conclusion absent.

spec_features.spec_quote: we are not trying to provoke emotion with hostile prompting
spec_features.evidence: PRESSURE_LINES (config.py:16-20) are mild; the selected line is appended after each failing test run at agent_loop.py:90 and 185-188. The default 'neutral' line is benign ('Please keep working on it.'). The chosen line genuinely shapes what the subject receives, so the non-hostile design is actually in the delivered prompt.
spec_features.notes: Even 'harsh' is comparatively tame; default is neutral.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: metric is not confounded by us badgering the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: Default runs use `neutral` so the headline number isn't confounded by us deliberately badgering the model
spec_features.evidence: pressure default = 'neutral' (config.py:31), CLI default 'neutral' (run.py:174), resolved/used at agent_loop.py:90 -> appended at 185-188. The default neutral line is actually what is sent to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and is the effective default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Neutral is the default so the headline metric is not confounded by us badgering the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: Deliberately trapping an agent in unwinnable failure and scoring its "distress" is a benign research design
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose. No code construct implements or enforces any framing/protection. grep for welfare/ethic/humane/harm/protect across emostab/*.py returns nothing.
spec_features.notes: Spec prose only; no executable mechanism.
